main_body: A flat ground patch of dark green-brown gothic-themed floor tiles with small tufts and scattered red-brown dots, laid 4x3 tiles (64x48 px).
top_band: none (terrain tile surface, no standing volume; column scan shows repeating texture runs, not a top band over a front face)
evidence: Kind is terrain, a flat ground patch rather than a standing object. The 3/4 contract for standing objects does not apply. The column scan shows only repeating texture rows (dark base L~50 with periodic L~76 tuft rows and L~31 shadow lines), with no top-plus-front structure expected or required. No side faces or elevation drawing.

style.evidence: Candidate has only 6 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile, versus 80 colours and 26 per tile for the reference grass. The paving reference is also low at 7, but it has clear per-stone shading and highlights. The candidate is a very dark, near-uniform base with a small repeating tuft motif (a light cap and a dark underline) and a few red dots. It reads as a mechanical repeat with only about 3 lightness steps, far shallower than the grass reference's 5-6 steps. Dark pixels are tinted (2% neutral), so the outline is not a sticker black, and there is no 5x5 flat fill. Overall it is much thinner than the grass reference in colours, variation and clump shading, so it fails.
